topic: Plane table surveying: principles and methods of plane tabling
source: survey251-350 updated.json (merged from old LEVEL 7 archive)

questions.q: 260. The types of survey in which field work and plotting proceeds simultaneously
questions.explain: Plane table surveying is unique because the map is drawn in the field while the observations are being made.

questions.q: 261. Plane table surveying is graphical method of surveying in which
options: field work and plotting proceeds simultaneously
plotting is done later while records are taken in field book
questions.explain: The primary advantage of plane table surveying is that the map is prepared in the field directly, eliminating the need for a separate field book.

questions.q: 262. Setting up the plane table consists of operations
questions.explain: Basic setup involves getting the board horizontal (levelling) and placing the plotted point exactly over the ground station (centering).

questions.q: 263. Plane table survey is considered good as compared to other survey since
options: chances to missing details are less
questions.explain: Since plotting happens while looking at the actual terrain, the surveyor is much less likely to omit important features.

questions.q: 264. A disadvantage of plane table survey is
options: It is heavy, cumbersome and awkward to carry
It can't be used in wet climate
details may not be available while redrawing to a different scale
accessories are likely to be lost
questions.explain: The large board and tripod make it physically more difficult to transport compared to a compass or a simple level.

questions.q: 265. Placing the table over the station such that the station plotted on sheet is exactly above the corresponding station on the ground is
questions.explain: Centering ensures the vertical axis of the plotted point and the ground station are aligned.

questions.q: 266. Orientation is the operation of keeping the table at successive stations such that
options: the position of the table at the station is parallel to the position it occupied at the previous station
the position of station plotted on sheet is exactly above the corresponding station on ground
the table is brought in a horizontal plane
questions.explain: Orientation ensures that every line on the paper remains parallel to its corresponding line on the ground.

questions.q: 267. The method of plane tabling generally adopted to obtain details and plotting inaccessible points is
questions.explain: Intersection plots points by the crossing of rays from two different stations, which is ideal for points that cannot be reached to measure distance.

questions.q: 268. In the intersection method of plane tabling the number of stations needed to be set up are
questions.explain: At least two known stations are required to create the intersecting rays for a single point.

questions.q: 269. Resection is the method employed for
questions.explain: Resection is specifically used to establish the location of the plane table on the map by observing known points.

questions.q: 270. The two point problem is
options: a case of resection method where no ray is required to be drawn from the proceeding station to the instrument station
locating the position of plane table by means of two visible well defined points
questions.explain: It is a resection technique where the table is oriented and located using two known points, often involving an auxiliary station.

questions.q: 271. The two- point problem as compared to the three point problem is
questions.explain: The two-point problem involves more steps and temporary setups compared to the three-point problem.

questions.q: 272. The three point problem can be solved by
questions.explain: Several methods exist to solve the three-point problem, including Lehmann's (trial and error) and Bessel's (graphical).

questions.q: 273. Three point problem is concerned with
questions.explain: This is a fundamental resection problem specific to plane table surveying.

questions.q: 274. The size of plane table is
questions.explain: Standard surveying plane tables typically measure 600mm by 750mm.

questions.q: 275. The process of aligning the plane table by rotating it in the horizontal plane to the corresponding lines on the ground
questions.explain: Rotation to align with ground features is the definition of orientation.

questions.q: 276. The triangle formed by joining the position of the known points on plane table survey is known as
questions.explain: In the context of the three-point problem, the triangle formed by the three known points is called the great triangle.

questions.q: 277. In case of resection method of plane table, the relation between great triangle and great circle are
options: the area of great triangle is more than great circle
the area of great triangle is less than great circle
the area of great triangle is equal to great circle
questions.explain: Geometrically, the circle passing through the three points (great circle) encloses the triangle (great triangle).

questions.q: 278. Strength of fix of a plane table is
options: accuracy in locating the position of instrument station by taking observation to three stations
fixity of table while solving two point problem
questions.explain: Strength of fix refers to how accurately the table's position is determined relative to the known points.

questions.q: 279. The fix of table is good when
options: the station is within the great triangle
the middle station is much nearer than other two stations
the angle subtended between two stations is not very small
questions.explain: A good fix requires geometry that avoids 'danger circles' where the position becomes indeterminate.

questions.q: 280. A poor fix of the table is
options: when station is within the great triangle
when station is near the great circle
questions.explain: If the instrument station lies on or near the circle passing through the three known points, the solution becomes unreliable.

questions.q: 281. The strength of fix' is poor when
options: the station is within the great triangle
the station is outside the great circle
the station is on the great circle
the station is within the great circle but outside the great triangle
questions.explain: The position is indeterminate if the station is on the circumference of the great circle.

questions.q: 282. The two point problem and three point problems are methods of
questions.explain: Both problems solve for the station's location and the table's orientation simultaneously.

questions.q: 283. The resection by two point problem as compared to the three point problem
questions.explain: Two-point resection is more cumbersome and usually less accurate than three-point resection.

questions.q: 284. If the plane table is not horizontal in a direction at right angles to the alidade, the line of sight is parallel to fiducial edge only for
questions.explain: Errors due to non-horizontality are minimized or eliminated when the line of sight itself is horizontal.

questions.q: 285. To orient a plane table without two inaccessible points, the method generally adopted is
questions.explain: The two-point problem is the specific procedure used to orient when only two points are available and distance measurement is not possible.

questions.q: 286. Which one of the following is not a personal error ?
options: the table not being perfectly leveled
the table not being perfectly central
the table not being perfectly clamped
questions.explain: All listed items (levelling, centering, clamping) are under the surveyor's control and are therefore personal/instrumental setup errors.

questions.q: 287. The method of plane tabling in which plane table is set only one station to take detail is known as
questions.explain: Radiation involves taking rays and distances to all points from a single setup.

questions.q: 288. Detailed plotting is generally done by
questions.explain: Radiation is the most efficient way to plot numerous nearby details once the station is established.

questions.q: 289. Radiation method of plane table survey is the best suited when
questions.explain: Since distances must be measured (usually with a tape/chain), it is best for short, clear paths.

questions.q: 290. In plane table instrument for horizontal & vertical measurement without chaining
questions.explain: A telescopic alidade is equipped with stadia hairs for distance and a vertical circle for slope angles.

questions.q: 291. The method most suitable for plotting in hilly areas is
questions.explain: Intersection is preferred in hills where measuring horizontal distance on steep slopes is difficult.

questions.q: 292. Intersection is preferred to radiation when
options: it is not possible to measure any distance
the points are too far and invisible
questions.explain: Intersection removes the need to physically reach the target point.

questions.q: 293. Actually which is not the method of plane tabling ?
questions.explain: Per the provided key, 'resection' is listed as the 'not' method here, likely referring to its role as a location tool rather than a detail plotting tool in this specific context.

questions.q: 294. The instrument used for centering the plane table accurately is
questions.explain: The plumbing fork (or U-frame) carries a plumb bob to transfer the ground point to the paper.

questions.q: 295. The orientation of the table is done by
questions.explain: The table can be oriented using a compass (magnetic needle) or by aligning a line with a previously occupied station (back sighting).

questions.q: 296. "Fiducial edge" is the working edge of
questions.explain: The bevelled ruler edge of the alidade used for drawing rays is the fiducial edge.

questions.q: 297. Which instrument is not used in plane table ?
questions.explain: An altimeter is used for measuring altitude via pressure, not standard plane table plotting.

questions.q: 454. The use of alidade is associated with the use of:
questions.explain: An alidade is a sighting device (either a simple ruler or telescopic) used specifically in plane table surveying to draw lines of sight on a map.
